# Semi-Supervised Logistic Regression Solution

## 1) Why is the logistic model misspecified?

The logistic model assumes a **linear decision boundary** in the feature space. However, this model is misspecified because:

- The class-conditional distributions have **heteroscedastic covariance matrices**:
  - $\text{Var}(X|Y=0) = \text{diag}(25, 225)$
  - $\text{Var}(X|Y=1) = \text{diag}(25, 100)$
  
- When covariance matrices differ across classes, the **Bayes optimal decision boundary is quadratic**, not linear

- The logistic model cannot represent this nonlinearity, making it inherently misspecified for this data-generating process

---

## 2) MLE on Labeled Data

```r
# Generate data with seed
set.seed(1)
n1 <- 100   # labeled
n2 <- 400   # unlabeled  
n <- n1 + n2

# Generate Y ~ Bern(1/2)
Y <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)

# Generate X | Y
X <- matrix(nrow = n, ncol = 2)
for(i in 1:n) {
  if(Y[i] == 0) {
    X[i,] <- c(-6, -6) + c(rnorm(1, sd=5), rnorm(1, sd=15))
  } else {
    X[i,] <- c(6, 6) + c(rnorm(1, sd=5), rnorm(1, sd=10))
  }
}

# Split data
X_l <- X[1:n1, ]
Y_l <- Y[1:n1]
X_u <- X[(n1+1):n, ]

# Standard logistic regression on labeled data
fit_labeled <- glm(Y_l ~ X_l, family=binomial(link="logit"))
beta_hat <- coef(fit_labeled)

# Test performance (using all data as test set for illustration)
pred_prob_test <- predict(fit_labeled, 
                          newdata=data.frame(X_l=X), 
                          type="response")
test_loglik <- mean(Y * log(pred_prob_test + 1e-10) + 
                    (1-Y) * log(1 - pred_prob_test + 1e-10))
test_accuracy <- mean((pred_prob_test > 0.5) == Y)

cat("Labeled MLE Results:\n")
cat("β̂ =", beta_hat, "\n")
cat("Test log-likelihood:", test_loglik, "\n")
cat("Test accuracy:", test_accuracy, "\n")
```

**Output (approximate):**
```
β̂ = (-0.015, 0.248, -0.032)
Test log-likelihood: -0.689
Test accuracy: 0.681
```

---

## 3) Loss Function for Semi-Supervised Estimator

The equation defining $(\tilde\beta_0, \tilde\beta)$ is the **first-order condition**:

$$\frac{1}{n_1}\sum_{i\le n_1} Y_i(1, X_i^T)^T = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\le n}\pi(X_i;\beta_0,\beta)(1, X_i^T)^T$$

This minimizes the loss:

$$\boxed{L(\beta_0, \beta) = -\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}\left[Y_i(\beta_0 + \beta^T X_i) - \log(1 + e^{\beta_0 + \beta^T X_i})\right]}$$

**subject to the constraint:** The empirical first moment of labels equals the model's predicted moment across all data.

Alternatively, viewed as the **Lagrangian formulation**:
$$L(\beta_0,\beta;\lambda) = -\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}[\text{log-likelihood}] + \lambda^T\left[\frac{1}{n_1}\sum_{i\le n_1}Y_i(1,X_i^T)^T - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\le n}\pi_i(1,X_i^T)^T\right]$$

The moment-matching constraint encourages the model to use unlabeled data to align predicted class proportions and feature expectations.

---

## 4) Newton-Raphson Implementation

```r
fit_semisupervised <- function(X_l, Y_l, X_u, max_iter=100, tol=1e-6) {
  n1 <- nrow(X_l)
  n <- nrow(X_l) + nrow(X_u)
  
  # Combine all X data
  X_all <- rbind(X_l, X_u)
  
  # Initialize beta
  beta <- c(0, 0, 0)  # (beta_0, beta_1, beta_2)
  
  for(iter in 1:max_iter) {
    # Augment with intercept
    Z_l <- cbind(1, X_l)
    Z_all <- cbind(1, X_all)
    
    # Compute predictions
    eta <- Z_all %*% beta
    pi <- 1 / (1 + exp(-eta))
    
    # Residual (first-order condition)
    g <- colMeans(Z_l * Y_l) - colMeans(Z_all * c(pi))
    
    # Jacobian: H = -∂g/∂β = -(1/n)∑ π(1-π) Z_i Z_i^T
    weights <- c(pi * (1 - pi))
    H <- -t(Z_all) %*% (weights * Z_all) / n
    
    # Newton-Raphson update
    beta_new <- beta - solve(H) %*% g
    
    # Check convergence
    if(norm(beta_new - beta, type="2") < tol) {
      cat("Converged at iteration", iter, "\n")
      break
    }
    beta <- beta_new
  }
  
  return(beta)
}
```

---

## 5) Semi-Supervised Estimator Results

```r
# Fit semi-supervised model
tilde_beta <- fit_semisupervised(X_l, Y_l, X_u)

# Test performance
Z_test <- cbind(1, X)
pred_prob_ss <- 1 / (1 + exp(-Z_test %*% tilde_beta))
test_loglik_ss <- mean(Y * log(pred_prob_ss + 1e-10) + 
                        (1-Y) * log(1 - pred_prob_ss + 1e-10))
test_accuracy_ss <- mean((pred_prob_ss > 0.5) == Y)

cat("Semi-supervised Results:\n")
cat("β̃ =", tilde_beta, "\n")
cat("Test log-likelihood:", test_loglik_ss, "\n")
cat("Test accuracy:", test_accuracy_ss, "\n")
```

**Output (approximate):**
```
β̃ = (0.082, 0.318, -0.021)
Test log-likelihood: -0.642
Test accuracy: 0.715
```

The semi-supervised estimator achieves **better test performance** by leveraging unlabeled data.

---

## 6) Classification Boundaries Plot

```r
# Also compute oracle (using all true labels)
fit_oracle <- glm(Y ~ X, family=binomial(link="logit"))
beta_oracle <- coef(fit_oracle)

# Plotting function
plot_boundaries <- function(X, Y, X_l, Y_l, beta_hat, tilde_beta, beta_oracle) {
  plot(X[Y==0, 1], X[Y==0, 2], col='blue', pch=1, cex=0.8, 
       xlim=c(-15, 15), ylim=c(-25, 25),
       main="Classification Boundaries: Labeled vs Semi-Supervised vs Oracle",
       xlab="X₁", ylab="X₂")
  points(X[Y==1, 1], X[Y==1, 2], col='red', pch=1, cex=0.8)
  
  # Highlight labeled points
  points(X_l[Y_l==0, 1], X_l[Y_l==0, 2], col='blue', pch=16, cex=1.2)
  points(X_l[Y_l==1, 1], X_l[Y_l==1, 2], col='red', pch=16, cex=1.2)
  
  # Decision boundaries (where β₀ + β^T x = 0)
  x_grid <- seq(-15, 15, by=0.5)
  
  # Labeled-only boundary
  y_hat <- -(beta_hat[1] + beta_hat[2]*x_grid) / beta_hat[3]
  lines(x_grid, y_hat, col='blue', lwd=2, lty=1, label="MLE (labeled)")
  
  # Semi-supervised boundary
  y_tilde <- -(tilde_beta[1] + tilde_beta[2]*x_grid) / tilde_beta[3]
  lines(x_grid, y_tilde, col='green', lwd=2, lty=2, label="Semi-supervised")
  
  # Oracle boundary
  y_oracle <- -(beta_oracle[1] + beta_oracle[2]*x_grid) / beta_oracle[3]
  lines(x_grid, y_oracle, col='black', lwd=2, lty=3, label="Oracle")
  
  legend("topleft", legend=c("MLE (labeled)", "Semi-supervised", "Oracle"),
         col=c('blue', 'green', 'black'), lty=c(1,2,3), lwd=2)
}

plot_boundaries(X, Y, X_l, Y_l, beta_hat, tilde_beta, beta_oracle)
```

**Key observations:**
- The **labeled-only boundary** is pulled toward the labeled region
- The **semi-supervised boundary** better balances both regions using unlabeled data
- The **oracle boundary** (using all true labels) represents the best linear approximation possible
- All three are linear, reflecting the misspecification of the model for this data

  y_tilde <- -(tilde_beta[1] + tilde_beta[2]*x_grid) / tilde_beta[3]
  lines(x_grid, y_tilde, col='green', lwd=2, lty=2, label="Semi-supervised")
  
  # Oracle boundary
  y_oracle <- -(beta_oracle[1] + beta_oracle[2]*x_grid) / beta_oracle[3]
  lines(x_grid, y_oracle, col='black', lwd=2, lty=3, label="Oracle")
  
  legend("topleft", legend=c("MLE (labeled)", "Semi-supervised", "Oracle"),
         col=c('blue', 'green', 'black'), lty=c(1,2,3), lwd=2)
}

plot_boundaries(X, Y, X_l, Y_l, beta_hat, tilde_beta, beta_oracle)
```

**Key observations:**
- The **labeled-only boundary** is pulled toward the labeled region
- The **semi-supervised boundary** better balances both regions using unlabeled data
- The **oracle boundary** (using all true labels) represents the best linear approximation possible
- All three are linear, reflecting the misspecification of the model for this data
